blocks.text: The chapter is framed as a prayer: it asks God to renew and make known his work, while remembering mercy in wrath. Its closing moves from trembling and quiet waiting in the face of crop and livestock failure to joy in God and confidence in God’s strength. Although the heading calls Habakkuk a prophet, independent evidence does not securely establish further details about his life or role.

Verses 3–15 portray God’s coming and victory with storm, military, cosmic, creation, and exodus-like imagery. Verse 13 says that God goes out for the salvation of the people and of “thine anointed,” but it does not identify that anointed figure. The chapter also contains difficult lines for which its surviving textual witnesses show variation, including verse 13; interpretations should therefore leave some conclusions open.
